index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure presents a comprehensive taxonomy of recommendation unlearning, structured as a hierarchical flowchart. The global layout is centered around a main root node labeled 'Recommendation Unlearning Taxonomy' in a gray rectangular box with bold black text. From this root, two primary branches extend downward: one leading to 'Input Unlearning' and the other to 'Attribute Unlearning', both represented in light blue rectangular boxes with black text. These two categories form the top-level classification of unlearning types.

On the left side of the diagram, within a dashed rectangular boundary, four colored headers indicate different perspectives for analyzing unlearning: 'From algorithmic perspective' (red), 'From parametric perspective' (yellow), 'From functional perspective' (blue), and 'From attack perspective' (purple). Below these headers are two additional boxes: 'Unlearning Target' (light blue) and 'Model/Scenario' (light yellow), suggesting dimensions for categorization.

The 'Input Unlearning' branch further splits into three subcategories, each in a light yellow rectangular box: 'Model-agnostic', 'Model-specific', and 'Scenario-specific'. Each of these then branches out into specific methods listed in gray rectangular boxes with black text and corresponding reference numbers in square brackets. Under 'Model-agnostic', the methods are 'Exact Unlearning [15, 55, 56, 57]' and 'Approximate Unlearning', which further subdivides into 'Reverse Unlearning [58, 105, 121, 122]', 'Active Unlearning [3, 14, 21, 66, 94, 118]', and 'Matrix Correction [65]'.

Under 'Model-specific', the methods include 'Bi-linear Recommendation [115]', 'KNN-based Recommendation [89]', 'Graph-based Recommendation [30]', and 'Knowledge graph-based Recommendation [107]'. Under 'Scenario-specific', the methods are 'Federated Recommendation [119]', 'Sequential Recommendation [117]', 'Session-based Recommendation [113]', and 'LLM-based Recommendation [39, 104]'.

The 'Attribute Unlearning' branch splits into two subcategories in gray rectangular boxes: 'In-training [24, 26]' and 'Post-training [18, 59]'. All connections between nodes are represented by solid black arrows indicating directional flow from general to specific categories. The visual hierarchy emphasizes a top-down classification from broad unlearning types to specific methodologies and scenarios. The color coding helps distinguish between major categories: light blue for primary unlearning types, light yellow for intermediate classification levels, and gray for specific techniques or scenarios. The diagram is clean, with clear text and consistent box shapes, facilitating easy interpretation of the taxonomy structure.
